title: Sections of line bundles of degree at least $2g-1$
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $C$ a proper smooth connected curve of
genus $g$ ([def-sc-genus]) over $k$, and $\mathcal L$ a line bundle on
$C$ of degree $d=\deg\mathcal L\ge2g-1$ ([def-sc-pic0]). Then
$H^1(C,\mathcal L)=0$ and

$$
h^0(\mathcal L):=\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal L)=d+1-g.
$$

proof.text:
The curve is connected in the sense of [def-sc-curves], hence has dimension one. Apply [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] to the line bundle $\mathcal L$: its dimension-one case gives
$$
H^1(C,\mathcal L)^{\vee}\cong H^0(C,\mathcal M),\qquad\mathcal M:=\Omega^1_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}.
$$
The same theorem makes these cohomology groups finite-dimensional and gives $H^q(C,\mathcal L)=0$ for $q\ge2$.

source.place: proof, first paragraph; Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves, Tag 0BS6, part (3), duality formula

proof.text: By [lem-sc-canonical-degree], $\Omega^1_{C/k}\cong\mathcal O_C(K_C)$ has degree $2g-2$. The dual of the invertible $\mathcal L$ is invertible by [lem-sc-invertible-dual]; the tensor product $\mathcal M$ is therefore a line bundle. Additivity of degree and its negation under duals follow from the homomorphism [def-sc-pic0]. Thus $\deg\mathcal M=(2g-2)-d\le-1$.

source.place: proof, second paragraph; Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves, Tags 0BS2 (6) and 0BS6 (2)

proof.text: Suppose $s\in H^0(C,\mathcal M)$ is nonzero. Since $C$ is integral, [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] (3) sends $s$ injectively to a nonzero rational section $s_\eta$. At each closed point $P$, its germ is in $\mathcal M_P$, so the local coefficient of $s_\eta$ relative to a generator of $\mathcal M_P$ lies in the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{C,P}$; by [def-sc-rational-section-divisor] its order is nonnegative. Hence $D:=\operatorname{div}(s_\eta)$ is effective and has $\deg D\ge0$ by [def-sc-divisor]. But [lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section] identifies $\mathcal M$ with $\mathcal O_C(D)$, and [def-sc-pic0] gives $\deg\mathcal M=\deg D$, contrary to Step 2. Therefore $H^0(C,\mathcal M)=0$.

source.place: proof, last paragraph, the negative-degree argument expanded using the divisor construction of lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section and Stacks Project, Divisors, Tags 02SF and 0BE6

proof.text: The isomorphism in Step 1 now gives $H^1(C,\mathcal L)^{\vee}=0$. This space is finite-dimensional by [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve], so $H^1(C,\mathcal L)=0$. Its cohomology in degrees $q\ge2$ vanishes by the same theorem. Consequently $\chi(C,\mathcal L)=\dim_kH^0(C,\mathcal L)$; [lem-sc-riemann-roch] (1) gives $\chi(C,\mathcal L)=d+1-g$.

source.place: proof, last paragraph; Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves, Tag 0BS6 (3), Riemann-Roch and duality
